title: Where the animals are: the world's cattle, sheep, goats, pigs and chickens on one map
excerpt: 35.3 billion farm animals for 8.1 billion people, mapped every 10 km. Chickens have multiplied 7.1 times since 1961, farm mammals outnumber people in 40 countries, and New Zealand has lost two thirds of its sheep.
seo_description: A world map of farm animals every 10 km: where cattle, sheep, goats, pigs and chickens live, and how the herds have changed since 1961.
header_alt: Title card reading 'Where the animals are' in black and barn red on cream, beside a world map colouring every 10 km square by its main farm animal: brown cattle across most continents, pink pigs over eastern China, dark blue buffaloes over northern India, green sheep in Patagonia, South Africa and Australia. Text: 35.3 billion farm animals for 8.1 billion people.
